espn-603999.headline: Stade de France has been Springbok property since 2013
beats: South Africa have won their last five Tests at Saint-Denis. The latest was 17–32 on 8 November 2025, and Rassie Erasmus is relishing a return to what he calls the "cauldron".

His one change to the starting side is Wilco Louw at tighthead, picked for his scrummaging, next to Ox Nche and Malcolm Marx. The Boks led Italy 45-0 at half-time, so the message is less about fixing and more about pushing. France, meanwhile, have injuries mounting at fly-half.

France are no soft target. They scored eight tries against Fiji, and their only loss in the Nations Championship was 32–34 in New Zealand. Win here and France climb to third in the world, with South Africa dropping to second behind New Zealand.
If the run ends, South Africa carry it to Ireland a week later.

espn-604000.headline: Argentina are short of hookers. Italy are short of wins.
beats: Julián Montoya failed an HIA in Dublin, and Leonel Oviedo was tested repeatedly in a game that ended with uncontested scrums. Both are doubts for Genova and Ignacio Ruiz is out, so Felipe Contepomi has called up Facundo Bosch, whose last cap came in 2021, and Bautista Bernasconi.

The back three is no healthier. Juan Cruz Mallía sprained a knee against Ireland, and Santiago Carreras and Benjamín Elizalde are injured. The fullback may be a new name, or Gerónimo Prisciantelli, the back-up fly-half.
Italy have lost five straight. Last week a depleted side let in nine tries to South Africa, all converted, and lost 7–66. A win here would lift them to 9th, above Wales and Fiji.
Argentina go to France next. Italy host Fiji, the other side still on nil points, which is a fixture they would rather not need.

espn-604001.headline: Rees-Zammit is smiling. Wales last beat New Zealand in 1953
beats: Wales have beaten New Zealand three times in 38 Tests, the last of them in 1953. Their last meeting, on 22 November 2025 in Cardiff, finished 26–52.
Louis Rees-Zammit beat 14 defenders against Japan last weekend and was player of the match. Wales needed all of it to win 28–21.

New Zealand put 43 points past Scotland and kept them scoreless after half-time at Murrayfield. Jordie Barrett and Will Jordan picked up injuries there and could miss Cardiff. New Zealand still sit level on points with South Africa at the top of the table.
A Welsh win by any margin lifts them above Fiji into ninth in the world. New Zealand would still be second, which is roughly the size of the gap Rees-Zammit is smiling at.

espn-604002.headline: Beating Australia by 23 cost England four players
beats: Feyi-Waboso's ankle has ended his autumn. Furbank, Chessum and Atkinson are rehabbing in camp with New Zealand in mind. That leaves Steve Borthwick three new starters in the backline and one at blindside.
Henry Pollock scored twice on the wing off the bench against Australia, and is unlikely to start there. With Tom Curry out for November and no Pepper or Underhill, the back row may need him more.

Japan lost 21–28 to Wales in Cardiff, near enough for a bonus point, and are the Pacific Nations Cup champions. A Japan win drops England to seventh, below Scotland and the Australia side they just put 45 past.
England have never lost to Japan in six meetings, the last 59–14. The selection is about New Zealand. The result still has to be about Japan.

espn-604003.headline: Three number eights down, and Fiji still to come
beats: Sean Jansen's knee gave out early in the second half of his home debut against Argentina, putting him alongside Caelan Doris and Jack Conan on the injury list. Uncapped Ulster back row David McCann has been called up to cover. Captain Dan Sheehan is also out, with concussion.

Fiji have taken no points from four championship games and conceded 54 to France last time out. Mack Hansen still warned this would be a stiff test, despite it sitting between Argentina and South Africa as the least daunting of the three.
Ireland are level on points with England and two behind France, so four tries matter as much as the win. A draw would also drop them below France in the world rankings.
South Africa come to the Aviva on 21 November, and Sheehan's 12-day protocol leaves him a doubt for that too. Ireland must win this one without the players they will need for the next.

espn-604004.headline: New Zealand put 43 past both. Now they swap notes
beats: Scotland lost 21–43 to New Zealand at Murrayfield on 7 November. Australia lost to New Zealand by exactly that score in October, and have now let in 50, 43 and 45 in their last three games.

The 45 came at Twickenham on 8 November. Harry Wilson admitted that "in our defence we weren't physical enough to slow their ball down", and Planet Rugby's Hamish Bidwell reckoned Scotland are closer to Australia's level, so this should at least be an even contest.
Sixth plays seventh, and win and Scotland go fifth in the world, above the England side that just put 45 on Australia.
Australia then stay in Britain for Wales, who sit one place and two points ahead of them in the table. They are still looking for a fly-half a year before they host the World Cup.

espn-604005.headline: The autumn England beat New Zealand ended a coach's tenure
beats: England beat New Zealand 33–19 at home on 15 November 2025. That autumn ended in a player review that cost Scott Robertson his job, and Dave Rennie has the side now.

Steve Hansen calls Rennie's side a "different team", built largely from the same players. They have scored 50, 43 and 43 in their last three, and kept Scotland scoreless after half-time at Murrayfield.

England have won three straight. The last was 45–22 over Australia, and it cost them Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Tom Curry for the rest of the autumn. One of the six call-ups is Max Hicks, born in Auckland and a Māori All Black in 2022, who could make his Test debut against New Zealand.
Win by 16 or more and England go up to third in the world. New Zealand are level on points with South Africa at the top of the table, and know better than most what losing to England can cost.

espn-604006.headline: Japan keep losing by a score. Scotland lose by 22.
beats: Japan went down 28–21 in Cardiff on 7 November, and Wales did not score the decisive try until the 69th minute. A fortnight earlier it was 34–28 to Fiji. That same 7 November, Scotland conceded 43 to New Zealand at Murrayfield, the same total Ireland put on them in March.
Wales won and Steve Tandy still admitted to a below-par performance. Japan crossed four times against Fiji and three times against Wales. The tries come. The finish does not.
Japan need one more score than they have been managing. Win by any margin and they go up to 9th, above Wales, the side that beat them a fortnight earlier.

Jack Dempsey, Scotland's No 8, is moving to Japan. He says the change will keep him fresh for a World Cup that Scotland open against Uruguay. Japan would like to show him what he is moving to before he arrives.

espn-604007.headline: Porter has had a year to think about the scrum
beats: South Africa won 24–13 at the Aviva Stadium last November, and Andrew Porter has spent almost a year stewing over Ireland's scrum that day. The Leinster loosehead has not played for Ireland since. His plan for the rematch is to "Swing at it".

The scrum behind him is thinner than he would like. Sean Jansen's knee has made it three Ireland number eights injured, captain Caelan Doris among them. Dan Sheehan, captain in Doris's absence, is on a 12-day return-to-play protocol after a concussion against Argentina.

South Africa have beaten New Zealand three times since August and put 66 past Italy. Rassie Erasmus still says they have to play much better. An Ireland win by any margin sends them below New Zealand in the world rankings.
Andy Farrell thinks the side that scored six tries against Argentina can be more ruthless. Last November, the scrum never gave them the chance.

espn-604008.headline: Eight defeats between them, and only one side gets to stop
beats: After four rounds, Italy and Fiji are the only two sides in the Nations Championship without a point. Italy sit last because they have conceded 20 more.

On 7 November Italy lost 66–7 to South Africa in Turin, nine tries all converted. On the same day Fiji let in 54 against France. The difference is October, when Fiji beat Japan 34–28; Italy lost to Japan 10–27 in July.
Win and Italy go up to ninth in the world, above Fiji, who come to Udine two places higher.
After this, Italy's next game is South Africa again, at the World Cup next October. They would like something else to remember in between.

espn-604009.headline: Argentina short of fullbacks, France not short of tries
beats: Juan Cruz Mallía sprained a knee in the 42–12 loss in Dublin, with Santiago Carreras and Benjamín Elizalde already injured. Felipe Contepomi called up Tobías Wade for Genoa and weighed moving his back-up fly-half, Gerónimo Prisciantelli, to fullback.
France put eight tries past Fiji in their last outing, 54–17. Before Argentina, they host South Africa, who have beaten them five straight times at the Stade de France since 2013.
Win by 16 or more and France go above Ireland to third in the world. All three of their wins since July cleared that bar, the narrowest 42–26 in Australia.
Argentina have won one of seven this year, with Italy still to come before Paris. After this, nothing until Canada at the World Cup in October 2027, which is a long time to look for a fullback.

espn-604010.headline: Australia arrive ranked higher and leaking 40-plus
beats: Australia have conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand and 45 at Twickenham in their last three games. They are still seventh in the world, three places above Wales, and two points below them in the Nations Championship.
England scored seven tries to three on 8 November. Afterwards Australia admitted they "didn't really fire a shot".

Wales beat Japan 28–21 with four tries, and Louis Rees-Zammit beat 14 defenders in it. They also lost 0–43 in South Africa in July, so the leaky defence is not the only one in Cardiff. A Welsh win by any margin lifts them above Fiji to ninth in the world.
Lose here and Australia have four straight defeats. Their next fixture is Hong Kong at the World Cup in October 2027, which is a long time to think about it.
